caption_used: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: The figure is a two-level donut (nested pie) chart showing the distribution of samples across two ambiguity-related measures, with the outer ring representing “Ambiguity Std” and the inner ring representing “Max Ambiguity.” The outer ring contains four slices with percentage labels on the ring: “Std: 0.0” in the darkest teal at about 49.0%, “Std: 0.47” in a medium blue at about 38.0%, “Std: 0.82” in a brighter blue at about 7.0%, and “Std: 0.94” in the lightest/bright blue at about 5.0%. The inner ring contains three slices in lighter blue shades with percentage labels: “Max: 1” at about 39.0%, “Max: 2” at about 47.7%, and “Max: 3” at about 14.2%. Two separate legends appear on the right—one titled “Ambiguity Std (Outer)” mapping the four darker blue shades to the Std categories, and one titled “Max Ambiguity (Inner)” mapping the three lighter blue shades to the Max categories; no slices are exploded or offset, and the segments appear arranged around the circle without an explicit ordering cue beyond their sizes.
